To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL28B and ss469415590 genotypes are predictive of response to PEG-IFNa/ribavirin treatment, and

IL28B and ss469415590 polymorphisms are predictive for treatment outcome in chronic hepatitis C patients, and that a combination of these polymorphisms is superior to a single polymorphism in predicting treatment outcome.
the combination of the two IFN lambda SNPs IL28B rs8099917 and ss469415590 predicts the treatment outcome of HCV genotype 3 infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new diagnostic tools for the individualization of antiviral therapies based on the prediction of virologic response.
the identification of novel predictive biomarkers in the treatment of chronic hepatitis C.
the prediction of the treatment response in chronic hepatitis C patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IL28B polymorphism has the strongest impact on the response to treatment in genotype 1 patients.
IFN-lambda polymorphisms are useful predictors for treatment outcome in patients with chronic hepatitis C.
the IL28B polymorphism rs12979860 and the IFN-L4 rs368234815 polymorphism are the best single predictors of SVR for HCV genotype 2 and genotype 3 infected persons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best predictor for SVR in patients with genotype 1,2,3,4 infected with hepatitis C is the combination of IL28b and IFN-lambda polymorphisms.
the IFN-lambda gene variants rs12979860, ss469415591 and rs8099917 are useful for prediction of SVR, and the rs12979860 and rs80999171 variants are also useful for prediction of relapse.
the best single predictor for treatment response is the IL28B rs8099917 SNP, the best combination of IL28Bs is the IL28A/IL28B haplotype and the best single predictor in genotype 3 is the IFN-L4 SNP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of the IL28B and the new IFN-Lambda4 polymorphism can predict the response to treatment with a very high accuracy of 71–90%.
IL28B/ IFN-L4 genotyping may help to individualize treatment decisions in HCV infected patients.
the combination of IL28b and IFN-Lambda polymorphisms can predict the response to antiviral therapies.
